the characterization of a cluster of Salmonellatyphimuriumgenes (phsBCDEF) that appears to be necessary for anaerobic H2S production from thiosulfates.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phs genes code for a membrane-bound thiosulfate reductase complex that catalyzes the anaerobic reduction of thiosulfate to hydrogen sulfide.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genes phsBCDEF encode the membrane-bound thiosulfate reductase of S. typhimurim, and that the gene OrfA encodes the soluble thiosulfate dehydrogenating enzyme.
phsBCDEF constitute the thiosulfate reduction operon of Salmonella typhi, and OrfA may be the first gene of the operon.
phsBCDEF are necessary for the conversion of thiosulfate to H2S, and that OrfA is necessary for the conversion to polysulfide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a cluster of genes, which we call phs, necessary for the reduction of thiosulfate to H2S in Salmonella typhmurium.
the genes for thiosulfate reduction in S. typhimurim are located on a single operon, phsBCDE, and that the gene for the terminal reductase is immediately upstream of this operon.

the phs genes are part of the thiosulfate-oxidizing system in S. typhimurim, and that the phs operon encodes an electron transport chain that may be analogous to the one encoded by the dms operon in E. coli.
